messages:
Sam: FYI incoming critical support ticket from Acme, p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s after today's runtime rollout. They reported first seen ~09:30 UTC.
Maria: Which rollout ID and canary percent?
Sam: rollout 2026-03-05-rt-v2.3.4, canary started ~09:12 at 10% per deploy bot.
Devon: Grafana slice: https://grafana.redwood/prod/rt/p99?var=service=runtime&from=09:00&to=10:30 shows p99 spike at the same time; p95 mostly flat.
Sam: Host-side telemetry shows a small cohort with long tail CPU stalls. Example trace: trace/0a7f9c3b — long kernel loader wait during generate.
Alice: Note: v2.3.4 changed kernel-selection precedence and enabled a latebinding path for small-batch cold-KV. Could be extra compile or fallback.
Frank: @Maria can you pull canary host list and quick CPU/context-switch metrics? Thinking narrow cohort.
Maria: Canary hosts: rtx-gpu-523, rtx-gpu-524, rtx-gpu-531-532. rtx-gpu-523 has 3x context switches and higher voluntary context switches around 09:12. IOwait looks normal.
Sam: Acme provided repro: single-stream chat with max_tokens=1024, stream=true, concurrency=2 for ~30s. We ran against canary and saw p99 ~900ms vs baseline ~210ms.
Devon: Paste exact request payload?
Sam: ```{
  "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
  "input": "<long prompt set>",
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "stream": true,
  "temperature": 0.0
}```
Alice: v2.3.4 flips a flag that lets kernel-selector pick latebinding kernels for certain sequence lengths. If a small fraction falls back to aten_slow that's a plausible root.
Frank: Kernel-selector logs on canary show occasional fallback->aten_slow at ~09:12 for the Acme requests.
Maria: grabbing /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log from rtx-gpu-523 and searching for "fallback->aten_slow" around 09:12; attaching snippet to thread.
Sam: I pulled traces from Acme request ids ace-11..ace-13. ace-12 shows ~700ms in kernel loader wait.
Devon: Mitigation options: rollback v2.3.4, hold canary traffic at 1%, tenant pin to rt-v2.3.3, enable strict kernel-selector, or temporarily bump Dedicated capacity.
Maria: I can pin Acme routing to rt-v2.3.3 immediately (no deploy). That should be instant.
Alice: We should bisect v2.3.4 -> isolate kernel-selector change first, then allocator tweaks, then latebinding flag. Kernel-selector is my top suspect.
Devon: I'll spin a test canary that reverts only kernel-selector change (test-ks-revert-001) and run the Acme workload for 30m. If p99 drops we have our cause.
Frank: Add extra debug logging to the kernel selector on the revert canary to capture decision rates so we can quantify fallback %.
Maria: Also added a sampling rule to capture 100% traces for Acme tenant for 1h to fill telemetry gaps.
Sam: Eng-oncall, please pause further rollout for 2026-03-05-rt-v2.3.4 to avoid full roll.
eng-oncall-bot: Deploy guardian: traffic freeze applied to rollout 2026-03-05-rt-v2.3.4 at 09:45 UTC. Oncall alerted.
Sam: Pinned Acme to rt-v2.3.3; customer reports p99 back to ~230ms at 09:50 UTC. Please prepare short customer-facing summary and RCA ETA.
support-bot: Customer notification sent (template) at 10:05 UTC.
Alice: Bisect plan: 1) revert kernel-selector only on canary; 2) run Acme profile 30m; 3) if improved, prepare hotfix to remove latebinding fallback and add stricter tests; 4) if not, revert next change.
Devon: Started kernel-selector revert canary now. Initial 10m metrics show p99 down to ~260ms on revert hosts. Will continue to monitor for 30-60m. :thumbsup:
Frank: Opened INC-8221 to recover some missing spans for 09:20-09:25 where sampling rollout missed traces.
Maria: Preparing follow-up JIRA for QA: add synthetic Acme workload to canary suite and add a small-batch latebinding scenario to regression tests.
Sam: Support: send the customer a concise update: paused rollout, pinned routing, bisect in progress, ETA for full RCA ~24h.
support-bot: Update dispatched to Acme at 10:05 UTC.
Devon: If kernel-selector revert holds, plan to ship a hotfix removing the fallback path, add stricter kernel-selection unit tests, and stage a cautious rollout with additional canary observability.
Maria: Also scheduling soak on rtx-gpu-523 variant to ensure no other regressions.
Frank: Nice work. Closing live escalation channel; will reopen if any regression reappears.
